name.ja: ルートヴィヒ・ボルツマン

overview.en: Ludwig Boltzmann was an Austrian physicist who developed statistical mechanics, providing a microscopic explanation for the macroscopic laws of thermodynamics. His statistical interpretation of entropy bridged the gap between Newtonian mechanics and thermodynamics.

early_life.en: Born in Vienna, Austria, Boltzmann studied physics at the University of Vienna, earning his doctorate in 1866. He was deeply influenced by the work of Maxwell and became a passionate advocate for the atomic theory of matter.

impact.en: Boltzmann's statistical mechanics provided the theoretical foundation for understanding thermodynamic phenomena at the molecular level. His famous equation S = k log W, relating entropy to the number of microstates, is engraved on his tombstone and remains a cornerstone of physics.

event.en: Earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna.
Published the Boltzmann equation and the H-theorem.
Formulated the statistical definition of entropy: S = k log W.
Derived the Stefan-Boltzmann law for blackbody radiation from thermodynamic principles.
Published 'Lectures on Gas Theory,' his comprehensive treatise on kinetic theory.

title.en: Further Studies on the Thermal Equilibrium of Gas Molecules

description.en: Foundational paper introducing the Boltzmann equation and the H-theorem for irreversible processes.

title.en: On the Relationship between the Second Law of Thermodynamics and Probability

description.en: Paper establishing the statistical interpretation of entropy with the famous S = k log W formula.
Comprehensive treatise on the kinetic theory of gases and statistical mechanics.

text.en: If you are out to describe the truth, leave elegance to the tailor.
Available energy is the main object at stake in the struggle for existence and the evolution of the world.
